english: Why, man, are you wet? -- I fell into the water. -- How did you fall? -- You see the duck by me(?); the duck fled the net(?) and the slippery mud. -- Don't bring the duck home, bring water. -- Mistress, don't scold us(?). -- Sit by the fire and I will give you warm milk. -- You are wetter than ducks.
uncertain: pótni mē smḗys: prohibitive with indicative góleti

english: Why do you put your own cutting-tool(?) into the stream? -- I give it to the grandson/ water-spirit(?). At the boundary in spring, may the crossers(?) drive the clouds from us. -- Does he want bronze? -- He wants the best. -- Now I give him my own spear. -- Don't give the spear; the fish are still at the boundary. -- Now I go to him with a song. -- The god hears it.

Grandmother, an otter woke me from the cave(?). The otter lived in the stream. It eats men's fish and they grumble. Standing in the water, the otter held the net with its teeth and fled. -- Did they catch it(?)? -- They did not. It still swims in the stream. -- I will look for it in spring. -- Look for it with stones, and do not go/throw against it.

Grandmother, ... I will cross over the ice. -- Don't cross. The ice is thin. -- My brother crossed it yesterday and did not sink. -- Yesterday the sun was warm this day(?). -- Now how do I go to the sheep? -- Go down by the bridge(?) and lean on the posts and the ice. -- Grandmother, you are wise. -- I, an old woman, have seen old ice.

The water carried me away. -- Who are you? -- I live still by the river. -- We are neighbours to you, (we) fishers(?). -- Today I am no fish(?). -- I saw a man in the stream and pulled him out. -- What shall I give you? -- Give me nothing. -- Don't forget me. -- I will not forget you. -- My brothers will not fight against you(?).

Why, father, is there a fire on the water at night? -- The fish come at night toward the fire. The fire over the water draws(?) them and I kill a heap. -- I saw a fish. It is big. Quickly it fled. -- Did you kill it? -- I killed it. -- Your mother will cook it at dawn.
